newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-BRAZIL OFFICIALS REVERSE BAN, RELEGATIONS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRAZIL OFFICIALS REVERSE BAN, RELEGATIONS.

text.p: Brazilian club Atletico Paranaense won a reprieve from a year-long ban from competition and two relegated clubs were reinstalled to the first division in a major about-face by soccer bosses on Friday.
Atletico Paranaense were barred from all competition for 360 days by the Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF) earlier this month after an alleged match-rigging scandal.
The decision sparked noisy demonstrations by Atletico fans. On Thursday Brazil's sports minister Pele added his voice to the chorus of protest, saying the decision was unfair.
On Friday, CBF directors met to discuss the case and issued a statement saying the club would be allowed to take part in the 1997 Brazilian championship.

The statement also said Fluminense and Bragantino, who were relegated from the first division in 1996, would be restored to the top flight. Both clubs had lobbied hard to take Atletico's place in the 1997 competition.
Three clubs which finished top of the second division last season would no longer be promoted, the note said.
